## Daeronnax

Daeronnax was an ancient red dragon who lorded over the Clan Daeronnax kobolds in the Stonelands during the 15 century DR.

Description
Daeronnax was a massive red wyrm who felt nothing but disdain for humanoids and adventurers, using their bodies to decorate the entrance to his lair. He experienced no fear of heroes, only disgust.

Location
Daeronnax laired in a volcanic magma-filled cavern beneath the Stonelands, surrounded by his Clan Daeronnax minions. Above his lair was an ancient Netherese tomb close to the surface, and deeper below in the Underdark was a drow outpost connected by portal to Sschindylryn.

Possessions

The great red dragon kept an impressive hoard of treasure in a non-molten corner of his lair, which included many relics stolen from the nearby Netherese tomb. Some of the items found included heartwood and festering mummy wrappings.

History
In the 1480s DR, a band of adventurers made up of Popkin Shortshanks, Jarus Brithandir, Helayna, Tristran of Daggerford, Kirina Aelorothi, and Liantor Stoneborn discovered an ancient tomb at the bottom of a crevasse in the Stonelands. They fought through some undead and found the deeper tunnels below it, eventually earning the attention of the Clan Daeronnax kobolds who launched an attack that scattered the interlopers. Jarus, Helayna, and Kirina were separated and lost in the caverns, Liantor was caught and killed by the kobolds, and Popkin escaped to the surface to get help. The unlucky Tristran was caught and taken alive, then delivered to Daeronnax who kept him chained up in the treasure pile as a snack for later.

The adventurers that Popkin recruited proved more than able, and they were able to fight their way through the Netherese tomb and into the Clan Daeronnax tunnels, rescuing her companions as they went. They finally found the lair where Tristran was kept, and overcame the threat of the massive red dragon to rescue him. The remaining kobolds were heartbroken and terrified, and Daeronnax's hoard was rummaged through before the dragon-slayers departed, possibly with one of his empowered dragonscales.

## Daluth

Possessions
He looted a plethora of magic from Karsus' Keep.

Abilities
As a dreadspell, he wielded borrowed arcane power.

History
Daluth was one of the dreadspells sent with Elryn to find and slay a Chosen of Mystra near Westgate two tendays into the Chaos of the Art in the . During the first leg of the trip, he had Uldus Blackram lead the way, while a knife to the man's back. During the first leg of their trip, Uldus Blackram was killed by Ilbryn Starym, an elven wizard they chanced upon.

Once they found the ruin, Karsus' Keep, Daluth helped loot it of valuables. The team of dreadspells then sought to bring down the whole ruin on top of two people they spotted, a self-styled god Azuth and the Chosen of Mystra they sought, by using all their looted magic to hurl destructive spells at them. Once their looted magic failed against Azuth, despite bringing down the ruin, they fled.

When Dread Sister Klalaera appeared and herded them back against Azuth, they were stopped partway by Umbregard and Starsunder, two mages that appeared suddenly. During the battle, after being injured by a beam that bared the flesh of his shoulder and the Dreadspells subsequently being reduced to just two, Daluth struck with a wand against Klalaera; upon death, her body to become animated by the power of Darklady Avroana. He was killed by a bolt of dark flame sprouting from her mouth, which left hardly anything of him.

## Dasumia

Dasumia, known as the Lady of Shadows, was a malevolent, Banite sorceress in the mid–8 century DR. She took over Galadorna and was served by the apprentice mage Elminster Aumar, a Chosen of Mystra, but ultimately revealed herself to be an avatar of Mystra herself.

Personality
She appeared to be a sadistic person.

Description
She was tall and sleek. She had proud, dark eyes, ivory skin, and glossy hair even longer than her long, long legs. Her features were pleasantly angular, and she moved with serene fearlessness. During Elminster's first meeting with her, she wore a gown and black boots, with no cloak.

Abilities
Dasumia was capable of working magic unnoticed, launching numerous deadly hanging and controlling spells even through a normal conversation. She also wielded the curious darkfire of Bane. Amongst other spells, she used one that made bolts of searing luminescence spring from her face, bodice, and hands, which Elminster could not wholly return; another of her spells created spinning bands of silver around her, which turned into attacking chains. She wielded some sort of spell-shield as well. Another spell created purple ricocheting lightning that spread from all around; another spell of hers conjured a cloud of green dust, which caused temporary petrification. She could also cast spells that were chained, setting one off as the previous was negated: in a spell-battle against Elminster, she launched a swarm of spinning blades, which released a snake-like whip upon nullification. This last spell could nullify a wall of force. Another of her spells hurled all of someone's bones out of their bodies, a killing spell akin to call bones.

Other spells she wielded at a later date included one that forced people to act according to her will, and another that caused an opponent to bloat out of his clothes, growing numb and heavy, with shifting limbs and many overlapping folds of flesh. Another spell of hers caused gravity to invert. She could also teleport to nearby locations, turn her blood to acid, and turn a helmed horror into a cone of deadly shrapnel.

Possessions
During her first meeting with Elminster, she was carrying a wand. She later wielded a rod she employed to explode the house of Holivanter. She also had a notable mask of unknown properties, if any.

Activities
Dasumia's day-to-day tasks were unknown, but she later became Queen of Galadorna. Her reign was largely one of absence.

Relationships
Dasumia was a Banite. One of her apprentices prior to Elminster had been Nadrathen. In Galadorna, she was obeyed by a number of helmed horrors.

History
Dasumia had had several apprentices down through the years. Three apprentices of them had kissed her unbidden; none of them survived her darkfire. One of her apprentices had been Nadrathen, who later became a Chosen of Mystra.

In mid-to-late winter of the, after liberating Buckralam's Starn, the Chosen of Mystra, Elminster Aumar, received a sign from his goddess calling on him to "serve the one called Dasumia". In Felmorel by spring of that same year, he learned there was a "Lady of Shadows" ruling lands east of that realm; his next vision from Mystra carried the message "seek me in shadows". After he fought and defeated the creature he named Silent Antlers at Tresset's Ringyl, Dasumia, unknown to him, took a hidden, magical scepter from the crumbling Ringyl.

Elminster finally met Dasumia shortly after, at the Riven Stone. Though he introduced himself as Elminster Aumar, the One who Walks, and as a Chosen of Mystra, she claimed that twoscore mages calling themselves that had come to her two months prior even during the snows, a dozen the month after, and one so far that month. But she also claimed that a dream-vision told her to seek an apprentice there. Elminster was aware that his silver fire at that moment countered a plethora of attempts to enslave and to leave slaying spells hanging on him. Nevertheless, he would become her apprentice as bidden.

Some of Elminster's punishments as Dasumia's apprentice included crawling on broken limbs and being strapped into a girdle of everhealing while being stabbed with poisoned and acidic weapons. While an apprentice, Elminster spent much time on his knees, praying to Mystra, which Dasumia saw. She also took a man as her lover, then tired of him, and turned him into a purple worm, leaving him stuck in the spits behind her stable; the man was later rescued by Elminster. She also bid Elminster create skeletons; he would create thirty-six. In the, Dasumia took Elminster to the tower of Holivanter, a rival mage, and commanded him to slay the man. When Elminster hesitated, Dasumia exploded the tower with a spell herself, and later used her own darkfire to punish Elminster; she held him by the shoulders, coming as close as she ever had with him. She then told him he'd serve her by slaying Nadrathen, a previous apprentice of hers, and another Chosen of Mystra.

Dasumia finally tested Elminster in a spell battle at the turn of spring to summer that year, which convinced her he was ready to battle Nadrathen. However, on the summer day in which they teleported to the House of the Unicorn in Nethrar to slay Nadrathen, it was Dasumia who struck the final blow instead of leaving it to Elminster. She then crowned herself Queen of Galadorna, the throne that Nadrathen had sought to usurp.

As Queen, she left Elminster to do all the work as her seneschal, and didn't use her power often enough to inspire terrified obedience, which made his task nigh-impossible; his decrees were ignored constantly, corruption and graft were rampant, and magic became a part of the intrigues and deaths: the land became a "nest of spell-hurling vipers" in the words of a local mage. Finally, one evening, she took the guards Ingrath and Delver to join her in a late-night ritual to Bane, where they'd become sacrifices. This prompted Elminster's final rebellion and he broke her control of the soldiers and tried to slay her. He managed to knock her out, but found himself disabled by her magic; after he tried to intercede with Mystra, she revealed that Dasumia was not actually a Banite, the ritual was modified, and that Dasumia, rather than a sorceress, was her own avatar. She then stole away with Elminster into the sky, leaving Galadorna to be destroyed before the end of the year.

Somehow, by spring of the, Dasumia had been captured by the Church of Shar and trapped in a sphere within the House of Holy Night in the Shaar, where her power was siphoned off by continuous human sacrifice. This also had the effect of inducing wild magic throughout the Realms, thwarting almost all spells.

## Daramos

The Daramos were a noble family from Thay. They were based in Thazalhar and Pyarados.

History
The family was one of the newest noble houses of Thay as of the mid–14 century DR. The family was based around Milsantos Daramos, the Tharchion of Thazalhar and a decorated warrior and commander.

As of, the family comprised Milsantos, his wife, their daughter Mantorra, and a son.

By, Mantorra had begun using the surname "Hennaflame" to disguise her lineage and to allow her to make her own way in the world. By that time, however, she had already used her family's connections to become an apprentice to Aznar Thrul, the Tharchion of the Priador and the Zulkir of Evocation, as well as to join the Kossuthan clergy at the Flaming Brazier temple in Bezantur.

Members
As Thayvian nobles, the Daramos were among the rulers of Thay. Family members were referred to with the honorifics of "Daeron"/"Daeronness" (literally, "noble-born"), or with "Sir"/"Mistress", "Your Excellency", or "Your Honor".

Notable members of the family included:
 Milsantos Daramos, the Tharchion of Thazalhar.
 Mantorra Daramos, Milsantos's only daughter and a member of the Order of Crimson Warlocks.

## Dark Arch

The Dark Arch, sometimes called Closeguard Bridge, was a bridge that connected the South Bank of Luskan to Closeguard Island in the River Mirar.

Structure
It was a short, arching bridge that continued from the Darkwalk on the South Bank. It had securable gates, and only members of the Arcane Brotherhood or of Ship Kurth were permitted to cross the bridge under normal circumstances.

Defenses
As of the mid-to-late 14 century DR, the Arcane Brotherhood had placed a secret ward on the Dark Arch that alerted them if anyone not affiliated with their faction were to cross it, and the Archmage Arcane Arklem Greeth had further strengthened its magical defenses. At the same time, the bridge had been rigged by Kurth engineers to be able to collapse in case of an attack.

History
When forces led by Deudermont and Lord Brambleberry attacked Luskan to drive out Arklem Greeth and the Arcane Brotherhood in the, a major turning point occurred when High Captain Kurth permitted their forces to cross the Dark Arch and Sword Bridge to attack Cutlass Island and the Host Tower of the Arcane by land.

## Darra de Aerindale

Lady Dowager Duchess Darra de Aerindale was an aged mage member of the Order of the Eternals who originally came from the world of Oerth and eventually settled on the world of Aphonion in the Kingdom of Stream's End.

Description
Lady de Aerindale had expensive tastes and wore a lush robe of purple and a perfectly curated collection of jewelry. Her immaculate appearance was legendary, as she never allowed anyone to see her improper or messy. At the age of 78, Darra appeared much younger than a human woman of her age would normally be. She kept aging at bay through magic concoctions and dyed her hair to hide the gray.

Personality
She was a woman of refined manners, proud, cultured, and respectable, to the level others could've perceived her as morose and stern. She was a lover of magic, considering spells to be intellectual feats and exercises – her favorite topic of discussion. Despite her seeming haughty appearance, Darra loved children, child-like adults, and sentient talking beasts.

Abilities
Darra was an accomplished wizard. One of her powers of note was an ever-present halo of immaterial ghostly eyes of differently-colored irises that gently looped around her head. The strange eyes allowed the Lady mage to see invisibility and improved her physical perception, making it almost impossible to surprise or ambush her.

History
Lady Darra de Aerindale's origins were on the homeworld of Mordenkainen – Oerth. Eventually, she was no longer welcome in her home. By some means, Darra found a way to the world of Aphonion, where she settled in the Kingdom of Stream's End, where she wed Lord Darius. Years passed as Darra prolonged her life through potions of longevity and application of hair dyes. She had one adopted son, Paramecium the Ferret, a sentient talking animal Darra had a soft spot for. Eventually, Lord Darius and Paramecium both passed of old age. Lady Darra's second husband, Larius, died in battle shortly before she turned 78. For the most part, since Larius's death, Darra remained alone, accompanied by her sentient animal companion, Piron the Ferret, the great-great-great-great-great-great...grand-nephew of Paramecium.

Despite her age, Darra did not care for retirement and sought to learn new things and share her magical knowledge and wisdom. In the late 14 century DR, the Order of the Eternals, a trans-dimensional guild for magic-users of impressive power, elected to hold its 1,238 annual Symposium in the city of Ravens Bluff on the world of Toril, in order to secretly investigate its unusually high levels of magical energies and planar incursions. The Symposium's attendees included Magi Paragon the Purple, one of the High Masters of the Order, and Darra de Aerindale, along with Piron the Ferret. All the guests stayed at Glittering Star Inn for the multi-day event. Paragon the Purple, however, was a victim of an opportunistic robbery with his cloak of the art and spellbook taken, and eventually returned with some aid from the wizardly heroes of the Living City.

Appendix
Behind the Scenes
The world of Aphonion mentioned in Impendant Symposium is a home campaign game-world created in 1977 by the module's author, Reynolds Jones.

## Darkwalk

The Darkwalk was a dangerous road in Luskan's South Bank.

Description
The road took its name from the haunted reputation of the Ruins of Illusk, through which it passed. Furthermore, many of Luskan's more notably dangerous alleyways branched off from the Darkwalk.

Geography
The road turned west from Aldever's Street at Captains' Close park and ran through the Ruins of Illusk to end at the Dark Arch bridge to Closeguard Island (and beyond that, to Cutlass Island).

History
As of the mid-to-late 14 century DR, the Darkwalk served as the boundary between the overgrown and undead haunted parts of the Illusk ruins on its north side and the safe and cleared part of the ruins to its south that had come to serve as burial grounds for rich Luskanites.

## Damara (wizard)

Damara was a wizard-king of the Dalelands in the mid-14 century DR.

Activities
Contemporaries described him as a ruler for good.

Relationships
He had a rivalry with the ogre Bonegnasher.

Possessions
He possessed the orb of dragonkind and ruled a castle in the Dalelands. Of note, he possessed a golden key that doubled as a flute or pipe. It opened a specific secret door under his castle, and that when blown could make a noise to which his orb responded. He laid himself to rest with an enchanted shield, a ring of protection, and a scroll of fireball and slow, as well as the orb.

History
Per the wizard Netheril's testimony, Damara was an ancient wizard who ruled a castle near Shadowdale using the power of the orb of dragonkind. According to a scroll the wizard provided, Damara had perished roughly around,It is assumed that the events take place between 1367 and 1372, the dates of 2 and 3 edition respectively. Per the materials in the adventure, he was slain 20 years prior. Thus, the rough date of his death is taken to be between 1347 and 1352. after his castle was attacked by the ogre Bonegnasher, who wanted the orb; as a last act, he hid the orb. His castle became known as the Tomb of Damara.

Appendix
Notes

Background
Damara is adapted from the wizard "Demara" in First Quest, a very similar boxed set, except the adventures are in Karameikos, Mystara, rather than the Realms.

## Dawan Pax

Dawan Pax was a legendary druid active in the North during the 15 century DR. He was known as the Hunter's Curse owing to his reputation for disrupting hunting events and for hunting hunters.

Description
He was graceful and athletic. Despite being quite large, he could move very quietly.

Personality
Dawan was a devoted and sometimes brutal defender of nature, and preferred the company of animals over people. He was vegetarian.

Activities
Dawan sought to protect animals from hunters, and failing that, to avenge them with great ferocity. He often used his wild shape powers to live among animals, and his preferred wild shape was that of a gray wolf in homage to an old friend. He was also known to use wild shape to adopt the form of animals slain by hunters when he pursued them for revenge. Alternatively, he would use magic to turn invisible when he hunted hunters.

Possessions
He had an item called the Soul of the Earth which allowed him to easily track other hunters.

He was known to carry flasks of an invigorating tonic made from peaches, mint, and ginger.

History
Dawan Pax was raised in an unremarkable orcish village where he learned to hunt alongside an old gray wolf, who lived in harmony with his village and came to be his closest friend. After the wolf was killed by outsiders for sport, Dawan vowed to hunt them down. This began his long career as a peerless hunter, a fearsome warrior, and a powerful druid.

He would come to travel across many lands, and never encountered a hunter who could defeat him. At some point, the Harpells of Longsaddle called on his aid when a group of particularly viscous hunters arrived in the Moonwood to hunt for pegasi. He made quick work of the hunters before bringing some of the injured pegasi to Longsaddle to establish a sanctuary. He was unaware that the Harpells collected such creatures.

By the late 15 century DR, Dawan Pax was a legendary figure. Some hunters did not even believe he truly existed, instead thinking that he was a boogeyman invented to scare them. Others believed that he was raised by animals, which was why he strove to protect them from hunters, while still others believed he was nothing but a mindless brute undeserving of any respect.

## Darya Scattertrail

Darya Scattertrail was an unlucky gnome druid adventurer from the High Forest druidic circle in Northwest Faerûn, active sometime before the late 14 century DR.

Possessions
Darya's adventuring gear included a pair of enchanted boots, later known as Scattertrail boots.

History
Sometime before the, Darya Scattertrail was initiated into the druidic circle of the High Forest. Several years later, she and her adventuring companions found themselves opposing a rogue Red Wizards of Thay who sought to tap into the dark powers of the Hellgate Keep. Despite the wizard's powerful sorcery, Darya's group used their knowledge of the terrain to trap the mage against an impassible ridge. The adventurers ended the Red Wizard's guards with ease, but the mage was not easy prey. He unleashed deadly spells that immobilized the gnome's troupe and summoned demons that devoured all the adventurers apart from Darya Scattertrail. Terrified, the druid used her boots' magics to flee, leaving her companions to their fate. Eventually, her panic subsided, leaving nothing but shame in Darya's heart. The woman threw all of her adventuring gear to the ground and forever left the High Forest. Sometime later, she was seen living in peace in a small village a day's ride from Silverymoon, repairing pottery for a fee of twenty coppers.

Darya's Scattertrail boots found their way into the hands of Dayne Lynneth, a merchant from Tyr's Eye plaza in the Blacklake District of Neverwinter in 1374 DR.

## Dame Guisarme

Dame Guisarme was a fighter-adventurer and a mercenary patron of the Elfsong Tavern from the city of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.

Description
Guisarme was a gold dwarf woman with pale skin, brown eyes, and long blonde hair. She kept her face clean-shaven and her hair styled. She wore a set of mundane half plate armor and was armed with a simple longsword and a shield.

Relationships
Dame Guisarme was barbarian Bombasto's traveling companion, with whom he seemed to have a flirtatious and friendly-antagonistic relationship. She thought the barbarian's schemes and ideas were crazy but ended up getting involved in them anyway, but not before receiving a compliment from Bombasto and responding to it with a slap.

History
In the, Dame Guisarme was a frequent customer of the Elfsong Tavern in the Eastway neighborhood of Baldur's Gate. She was often seen dining or enjoying drinks with her mercenary adventuring companion, Bombasto. They liked to discuss the Flaming Fist mercenaries and commander Liara Portyr's inability to stop the rampant murders in the Gate. Dame Guisarme offered Commander Portyr her services but, evidently, was turned down. Guisarme was sure that the Flaming Fists would eventually fail to stop the murders and Liara Portyr would end up asking Guisarme's help.

One of Bombasto's adventures was his and Dame Guisarme's stand against hobgoblin raiders who held a wagonload of beer. Bombasto was thirsty and suggested the adventurers trade a wagonload of donkey shit for the hobgoblins' beer. Despite Dame Guisarme considering the idea crazy, Bombasto went on pushing a wagon of manure off a hill. It rolled down and pushed the hobgoblins' cart of beer forward, slaying in its place. Guisarme grabbed the beer wagon down in a ravine.

During their time at the Elfsong Tavern, Bombasto and Guisarme contemplated accepting a job in East Chult, guarding extractive safari out of Fort Beluarian with bonuses paid to all survivors.

## Danzo Arkwright

Danzo Arkwright was the dwarf in charge of the Sword Coast Couriers in the Rivington neighborhood of the Outer City of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.

Description
Danzo was a tan-skinned gold dwarf with blue eyes and chestnut hair. He kept his face clean-shaven.

History
In the, Danzo Arkwright worked as the postmaster of the Sword Coast Couriers. However, his work was stressful as the region was affected by a looming threat of a war with the Cult of the Absolute, which led to some of the carriers being killed, letters being undelivered, and the loss of courier dogs. Trying to deliver letters in a timely manner, Danzo employed a small flock of carrier pigeons; however, that also proved to be a challenge when something started killing the birds off, and more letters were undelivered, including Danzo's personal correspondence. The said correspondence was Danzo's communications with Roah Moonglow, a Zhentarim cell's leader in Baldur's Gate. Danzo was to deliver an iron flask that was supposed to be smuggled into the city from the Waukeen's Rest Zhent cell for the Vanthampurs, and as that shipment was lost, the noble family was lost as a customer. Another letter was sent out to Gomwick, one of Danzo's couriers, but the warning message never reached the man. The reason for the pigeon mail disappearances was Tara, a Waterdhavian tressym, and a long-time companion of Gale Dekarios. The winged cat preyed on delicious pigeons and cared naught for the missing letters.

## Daviol

Daviol the Frozen was an adventurer and the first owner of the pair of Aurilite magic boots – the Frost's Embrace, who lived some years before the mid 14 century DR.

History
Daviol, soon to be known as Daviol the Frozen, was an adventurer who was betrayed by his troupe over a sack of gold. He was left to die of exposure while trekking across the Great Glacier. As he was dying amidst the frigid wasteland, he uttered a curse with his last breath. The curse reached the year of Auril, the goddess of winter. She granted him a boon of a pair of enchanted boots that protected his bare body against the extreme cold of the glacier. Daviol's new boots of the north received the name of the Frost's Embrace. Using the boon, Daviol crossed the frozen wastes in search of his treacherous companions, finding them in the safety of the closest tavern. The revenge was served and Daviol's bloodlust was sated. From there, the adventurer resumed his travels across the frozen north never to be seen again.

## Daransa's Moontouch

Daransa's Moontouch was a highcoin pleasure-house in the city of Suzail in 1348 DR.

Location
Located on a street off the side of the Promenade, the Moontouch was situated above several bawdy clothing women's clothing shops that sold expensive hats, gloves, gowns, and lace adornments. Two public staircases lead up to the business.

Structure
The building has protective magics cast over it, protecting it from scrying by even Cormyr's powerful War Wizards.
Interior
The rooms of the Moontouch were luxuriously furnished, with a richly paneled parlor lined with silk draperies and tapestries depicting vivid scenes of lovemaking. The parlor also sported a couch and a tea table.

Services
Being a high-end pleasure-house, the Moontouch offered patrons the service of highcoin girls. It also offered warm broth and tea to clients.

Reputation
Around 1348 DR, the Moontouch was considered to be one of Suzail's finer pleasure-houses.

Inhabitants
Beyond the namesake proprietor Daransa and her highcoin girls, the Moontouch employed a large and imposing male door guard.

History
Sometime around the, Princess Alusair Obarskyr snuck out of Castle Obarskyr late at night, seeking to pass on to Lady Daransa a coded message from the Harper Dalonder Ree. She was shadowed by a pair of War Wizards, Baerent Orninspur and Mrask Tallowthond, who had been tasked by Royal Magician Vangerdahast with watching over her. When they rounded a corner and found Alusair heading into the Moontouch, the pair stopped and gawked in disbelief.

Mrask considered if they should follow her in, but Baerent quashed the notion, arguing that Alusair would recognize his face and wouldn't be convinced that the War Wizards had come to the pleasure-house to slake their lusts. This would result not only in their cover being blown, but the two likely receiving some bruises and door guard sicked upon them. The two came to the agreement that they should try to eavesdrop from afar using scrying magic, but were shocked to find the Moontouch had warded against them.

Daransa warmly greeted Alusair, not recognizing her as the princess, offering her hospitality. Flustered at first by the graces of Daransa, Alusair passed on the coded message, "Three pearls have been lost, but one is now found." With this Daransa finally recognized her for who she was and kissed her fingertips, promising her she would always be welcomed at the Moontouch. As she exited from the pleasure-house, focused more on being fast than stealthy, she caught a glimpse of Baerent before he could turn his back on her and recognized him. As she fled into the night, Alusair cheerfully cried out to them with a smile, "Fair evening, you filthy spies".

Baerent ordered Mrask to tail her while he stayed behind to confront the Moontouch. When the guard refused to stand aside, holding a sword at the ready, Baerent cast a spell to temporarily paralyzed him and then swung wide the door into the parlor. Inside he was confronted by none other than the legendary Dove Falconhand. Baerent attempted to bluster out an excuse that he was intending no harm, but Dove berated the War Wizard. To her it was obvious that he was intending not only to interrogate Daransa as to what Alusair was doing at the Moontouch, but to learn how the pleasure-house could block a War Wizard's magics and intimidate them into never doing so again. Fearful of challenging one of the fabled Chosen of Mystra, the War Wizard left Daransa's Moontouch after Dove threatened his life, promising to never bother the women of the establishment and to refrain from telling Vangerdahast anything about what transpired.

## Darstil Vurusk

Grand Arcanist Darstil Vurusk was a powerful wizard and senior officer of the Night Brigade gang in Wheloon Prison in Cormyr in the late 15 century DR.

Description
Darstil had pale skin and short messy dark-brown hair.

Personality

The Grand Arcanist was thoroughly detached from conventional morality and only had a tenuous connection to reality. His main passion in life was his magical experimentations, which usually involved maiming, tormenting, and killing people and animals, to an extent that bothered even his fellow gangsters. He found his mistress Storna Harnwood unbearably stoic and restrained, and he believed that one should hurt the innocent while cackling wildly and enjoying life, not silently enduring it.

Possessions

Among his treasures were his bespoke gloves and bracers of magic and method, as well as the cranium sphere, the cold of night and Lesser Oblivion.

Activities

Despite being completely unhinged, Darstil was an exceptional wizard, able to perform astounding feats of magic. Much of his passions were devoted to his laboratory work, which involved magically, surgically, or psychologically mutilating various people, animals, and monsters in highly creative ways that sickened even the Night Brigade. He also took time to train other members of the Night Brigade as wizards, and used his talents to create servile monsters that spied upon the rest of the prison for the gang. Despite being a leading figure, he was mostly ambivalent about the rest of the gang and resented actually working with them, since it took him away from his personal projects.

History

Darstil became a leading figure of the Night Brigade gang, though he spent most of his time locked in his tower. He tortured and killed all sorts of people and creatures brought to him, including having an elaborate maze built that had no accessible exit. As a powerful wizard in Storna Harnwood's pocket, and a generally terrible person, the Riverside Rats targeted him for assassination. Wyshbryn Saldar sent a team of allies into the tower to slay him, and though they got stuck in the maze for a time they eventually escaped and put the mad mage down.

## Darstil's Tower

Darstil's Tower was the home, laboratory, and stronghold of the wizard Darstil Vurusk, Grand Arcanist of the Night Brigade in Wheloon Prison during the late 15 century DR.

Activities

Darstil Vurusk used his tower as a laboratory to test his ideas upon living creatures. He was exceptionally skilled at twisting the minds and bodies of his victims, pushing them to their limits before they perished. Darstil was utterly devoted to his foul work, and was rather dismayed at how his fellow Night Brigade members were put off by it. He only reluctantly assisted the gang with mundane, non-insane projects, though was quite happy when the two goals overlapped, such as creating bespoke twisted monsters that the gang used to spy on the city. Most of his creations were dumped in an elaborate maze beneath the tower, where they would run about endlessly before either starving to death or slaying each other.

History
When the Riverside Rats began their counterattack on the Night Brigade, Wyshbryn Saldar took special interest in the Grand Arcanist. As the source of much of the gang's magical expertise and firepower, Darstil was a key target for the wererats to take out. He sent a team into the tower through the front door, and they nearly assassinated the mad mage, only to be caught and teleported into his laboratory maze. After a perilous fight through the maze and past his guardians, Darstil Vurusk was finally put down for good, sparing Wheloon Prison his presence.

## Daerdatha

Daerdatha "Darkspells" was a drow sorceress involved in the infiltration of Scornubel during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

Description
Daerdatha changed spell-spun disguises often. Even close associates were not sure what she actually looked like.

Personality
Daerdatha was forceful, decisive, practical, but above all ruthless, willing to eliminate her own associates without even a second thought over the most trivial signs of hesitation.

Abilities
She was a sorceress, with enough abilities to pass for a cleric. She knew at least one spell that transformed its targets permanently into different shapes, which she used to create disguises for her fellow drow. She could directly affect the minds of her fellows, in some cases, sending not just commands but memories, and even painful admonishments, apparently being able to even grant that power for other people to execute on her behalf. One of her spells allowed her to mind-touch people, even through underlings in her command, lessening risk to herself. Another spell allowed her to make heads explode.

Possessions
She carried a crown of sorts, which she used for some magic. It was highly likely the crown was enchanted.

Activities
Daerdatha was a central figure in the infiltration of Scornubel during the mid-to-late 14 century DR. She likely trained some of them.

Relationships
The sorceress had personally recruited Anlaervrith Mrantarr to the infiltration of Scornubel, and kept close tabs on her, using magic to force commands into her mind at times.  She was also in contact with several other drow in the infiltration, including the one impersonating the husband of Anlaervrith's assumed identity, and the warrior Quztyr.

History
At some point prior to Dove Falconhand's investigation of her drow infiltration of Scornubel, Daerdatha had recruited a number of drow, including Anlaervrith Mrantarr, to serve as spell-changed infiltrators in that city.

On the night they were to attempt the taking of Halonder Eldeglut and his wife Iyrevven Eldeglut, Daerdatha discovered Anlaervrith Mrantarr had been supplanted by a different drow; when she had Quztyr, one of her warriors, attempt to mind-ream her, he was struck senseless by blowback. She immediately had him slain by his fellow Nuelvar Faeroenel. Linking her mind with that of several of her fellows by means of her crown, she was able to glean that the drow was Qilué Veladorn, one of the Seven Sisters and a Chosen of Mystra. She determined then the best way to deal with her while preventing divine vengeance was to break her wrists, gag and blindfold her, and finally throw her into the river to drown and be eaten by fish.

After the Chosen was hurled into the River Chionthar, Nuelvar Faeronel sighed with obvious loss, leading to her snap decision to explode his head on the spot.

Rumors & Legends
When deciding on how to kill Lady Veladorn, Daerdatha made reference to a decree then, that "no more drow blood shall be spilled in this city", thus making it a requirement to kill her bloodlessly. This was likely a ruse, as she had moments before had one of her warriors slit another's throat, and killed that warrior immediately after her execution by making his head explode. Both deaths almost certainly spilled some amount of blood as a result.

## Darrigo Trumpettower

Darrigo Trumpettower was a nobleman of Athalantar in the 3 century DR.

Appearance
He had a bristling moustache. By, he had come to rely on a cane.

Personality
The man was brave and lusty.

Relationships
He was the uncle of Peeryst Trumpettower and an elder of the Trumpettower family. He had been married at least twice; his second wife liked violent foreplay. He had no allegiance to King Belaur Aumar or the Magelords of Athalantar.

History
Darrigo had gotten married for the first time in the "Year of the Gorgon Moon", having been sober for that marriage. No such year existed in the Roll of Years.

On, the elder Trumpettower was downstairs from the bridal suite after the marriage of Peeryst, his nephew, and Nanue Glarmeir, his bride. He mistook some of the noises caused by an invasion of the Moonclaws thieving gang invading their suite for possible play from the newlyweds, but eventually heeded a cry for help, and if a little slowly, he came to their aid. He quickly removed the thieves from the suite upon arrival.

By, Darrigo had become a farmer, and come to use a cane; the sorceress Myrjala Talithyn was cornered by armsmen on that year in his farm, where armsmen got in despite his objections. A priestess of Mystra called Elmara (who was actually the disguised prince Elminster Aumar) then came by; he tried to bar her way, warning her that the armsmen were bloodthirsty, but she went around him and disabled them, rescuing Myrjala. he received a handful of gems from her, and afterwards, when a final armsman tried to kill her after surviving her attack, Darrigo finished him off.

Darrigo Trumpettower finally took the side of the rebel Knights of Athalantar openly, once they stormed the castle as part of Prince Elminster Aumar's attempt to overthrow his uncle, Belaur Aumar, the king, after Nanue was injured by a recklessly charging Jansibal Otharr's sword; he told Peeryst to bind her wounds and pursued Jansibal. After a Knight slew Jansibal, Darrigo recognized Helm Stoneblade, and decided to stand with them, immediately turning on Thelorn Selemban, who had tried to help him with Jansibal Otharr.

His cheek was sliced in combat soon after; he would pay with his life soon enough.

Rumors & Legends
It was said that Darrigo Trumpettower had hurled all of the Moonclaws thieves out of his nephew's bridal suite while the newlyweds consummated without noticing the tumult, which was an embellishment.

## Dave Arneson

David Lance Arneson (/ˈɑːrnɪsən/; October 1, 1947 – April 7, 2009) was an American game designer best known for co-developing the first published role-playing game, Dungeons & Dragons, with Gary Gygax, in the early 1970s. Arneson's fundamental early role-playing game genre work pioneered now-archetypal devices, such as cooperative play to develop a storyline instead of individual competitive play to "win"; and adventuring in dungeon, town, and wilderness settings as presented by a neutral judge who doubles as the voice and consciousness of all characters aside from the player characters.

## Daffyd Heights

The Daffyd Heights, also known as the Llyrath Highlands, was a rugged ridge of mountains rising from the middle of the Llyrath Forest on the south side of the island of Gwynneth in the Moonshae Isles.{{Cite digital book/Darkwalker on Moonshae||4}

Description
The crest of the mountains was sometimes described as the spine of the Llyrath Forest, with the peaks rising  above the trees. The steep climb up the mountains took travelers from the dense oak and pine groves at their base through a region where outcroppings of stone began to outnumber the trees until the steep and invisible trails upward began to follow the winding crest of the mountains. Here the craggy path was barely wide enough for horses to travel in single file and sheer precipices dropped away on either side, making the journey treacherous and leaving travelers exposed and visible from miles away. The path would sometimes dip between rocky peaks, creating narrow notches lined with clumps of rock and small pines that were ideal for ambushes.

Geography
The mountains dominated the eastern reaches of the Llyrath Forest. The main ridge was characterized by sheer stone peaks with valleys running down into the woods, while the intermediate ridges were covered in dense pine groves that occasionally opened onto upland meadows.{{Cite digital book/Darkwalker on Moonshae|?|5} At the base of the foothills were sheltered and pleasant vales.

History
When Kazgaroth returned to the Moonshae Isles in the, he emboldened the firbolgs of Gwynneth, promoting a group to establish themselves in the Daffyd Heights from where they attacked travelers within the forest. They were discovered and tracked by a hunting party led by Tristan Kendrick, but the firbolgs would ambush the hunters in the highlands: they killed Tristan's protector, Arlen, and forced the remaining hunters to flee.

Inhabitants
Some isolated cottages of lumberjacks and their families could be found around the base of the mountains.

## Darkwalker kin

Darkwalker kin were inhabitants of the Moonshae Isles who were believed to be descended from Kazgoroth. They lived with the sensation that their souls were divided into a normal portion and a bestial portion, which did not mesh easily.

Abilities
Their wild soul enhanced their strength and gave them an intimidating presence, while the primal power in their blood could grant them regenerative abilities. As with lycanthropes, they were vulnerable to silvered weapons, which burned them if touched.

They could freely shapechange between their normal humanoid form and that of a wolf. Individuals with the experience to bring their divided souls into harmony were able to assume a nightmarish hybrid form akin to that of a werewolf.

Members
Darkwalker kin were most notably shifters, who were referred to as having the "blood of the Darkwalker". Aside from shifters, humans were most likely to be Darkwalker kin, although it was conceivable that half-elves or elves could also be among Kazgoroth's descendants. Regardless, they tended to avoid civilization and favored life in the wilderness. Such Darkwalker kin grew up hunting and fighting in the wilds, leading them to master pack-oriented tactics as well as to hone their senses and instincts as sharp as those of beasts. Those with good hearts came to revile their feral ancestry, and so secluded themselves even from their own kind as they sought ways to bury their dark lineage.

## Dark Stag

Dark Stag was the local Herald stationed in Silverymoon, the Gem of the North, in the late 14 century DR. By the, the title was held by a mature woman of sharp wit who—after leaving behind the life of an adventuress—went against the typical notion of a bookish, elderly Herald. Doing her part to help maintain the city's laws, peace, and quiet, Dark Stag occasionally involved herself even in backstreet affairs.

Description
At some point, the Dark Stag of the late 14 century DR ventured into the Underdark, where she took sick with a strange disease. This devastated her tall body and, ultimately, was the catalyst for her retirement from adventuring. By the days of her tenure in Silverymoon, however, Dark Stag had begun to use a hat of disguise to modify her outward appearance—sometimes seeming an attractive man, but, most often, simply taking a more alluring, younger shape.

Abilities
Dark Stag was highly skilled in deductive reasoning and shrewd observation. So capable was she that the Heralds recognized her abilities, regarding her as one of the organization's best when it came to such matters.

Possessions
The Silvaeren Herald did not only rely on her hat of disguise. She was also known to keep two more pieces of magical equipment: a hand of the mage and a ring of feather falling.

Activities
During the days when fair Alustriel, the Lady Hope of Silverymoon, ruled that great city of the North, Dark Stag was considered one of the High Mage's closest confidantes. For this reason, Dark Stag—and other advisors of similar caliber such as Taern Hornblade—often met and conferred with Alustriel in the morning, soon after dawn.

Even when the mantle of rulership was passed to Taern Hornblade in Alustriel's stead, the working relationship between High Mage and Herald continued; he paid Dark Stag handsomely for any information she gathered and shared with him. To this end, she took to the streets of Silverymoon while using her hat of disguise. Adopting myriad parts amidst the night's revelries, Dark Stag learnt much about strangers and locals in equal measure.

Relationships
Beyond her membership among the Heralds of Faerûn, and even outside of her collaboration with the High Mages of Silverymoon, Dark Stag made many disreputable allies when she was an adventuress. Even after she retired, they continued to communicate, becoming a vast web of contacts.

History
Once in her life, Dark Stag was the target of a deadly ambush. Thanks to the assistance of an amiable wizard, however, she managed to escape; the mage briefly turned her into a sword, which allowed the pair to sneak out.

## Dagdar

King Dagdar was ruler of the Kingdom of Moray on the island of Moray in the Moonshae Isles during the early-to-mid–14 century DR.Canon sources identify Kimball as the royal family of Moray, however it is not stated if King Dagdar is a member of this family.

Description
He had a large, bear-like build. His arms were as thick as the legs of other men and were covered in thick, black hair. His black hair was worn long around his shoulders and down his back while his face was concealed beneath a huge, black beard. He spoke in a booming voice.

Personality
Dagdar was crude and boastful. He was incredibly proud of his people and his kingdom, and loved to spin enthralling tales about the places in his realm. He dismissed most of the threats to his realms, including orcs and trolls, as mere nuisances.

He enjoyed hunting, and kept a pack of well-trained moorhounds for his hunting trips.

Possessions
When he embarked on a hunting expedition, he traveled with a number of hunters, houndmasters, and enough retainers to fill out six chariots.

Relationships
His son and heir was Dynnegall. It was speculated that he might have been descended from one of the fallen sons of the maiden of Highpeak.

He hated the Northmen of the northern Moonshaes. He also had little respect for the other Ffolk realms of Callidyrr, Corwell, and Snowdown, whom he saw as too soft. That said, he was grateful to King Bryon Kendrick of Corwell for helping to repel a Northmen invasion in the 1320s DR, although he was hesitant to admit this aloud.

History
Late in his reign, he hosted the sage Elminster in his realm and sought to show him a good time. He invited the sage to join him on a hunting expedition, which took them south of Dynnegall to hear the wailing of the maiden of Highpeak.

In the, he led a rare assault against the Northmen by attacking the village of Trondhelm in Oman. He died during this campaign and was later succeeded by his son as king.

## Dagus

## Darkfyre

The Darkfyre was a magical focus used by the Ancient Ones, who were drow servants of Zaltec in Maztica, into which they fed the hearts of those who had been sacrificed on Zaltec's altars.

Description
It was composed of a caldron filled with a black liquid that glowed with a dark light. It could also manifest as an infernal blaze that emanated a red light. When the leader of the Ancient Ones, an ancient drow known as the Ancestor spoke the word 'Kizzwryll' and the Darkfyre would move in its caldron. It would also move when it was being fed with victims.

The Ancestor himself had a seat above the Darkfyre. The Darkfyre emanated heat.

Use
The 'Darkfyre was supplied every night by the Harvesters, who were young drow and also servants of Zaltec. Through teleportation, they brought the hearts from victims that had been sacrificed to Zaltec from across Maztica to the Darkfyre and fed them into the focus, in order for Zaltec to consume them. The Ancestor also sometimes fed the living into the Darkfyre as well. Zaltec gained power from the feeding of hearts to the Darkfyre.

The Ancestor also used the Darkfyre in order to prophesy the future, and it was through the Darkfyre that he learned that Erixitl of Palul needed to be killed in order for their plans of domination over Maztica to be realized.

The Viperhand cult, who were zealots of Zaltec, were also formed using the power of the Darkfyre.

History
Rockfire
According to dwarven legend as told by Luskag of Sunhome, the Darkfyre was the cause of the Rockfire cataclysm that destroyed the Underdark between Faerûn and Maztica, as well as much of the Underdark beneath Maztica. Supposedly, the drow and underdark dwarves were fighting a war, and during the war, the drow maintained the Darkfyre as a magical focus into which they fed the bodies of their enemies in order to increase its power. But they lost control of the Darkfyre, and by its own will, it grew into becoming a force of massive destruction that consumed entire nations as it spread through the Underdark caverns.

Recent History
In 1361 DR, the Ancestor summoned hell hounds from Zaltec's realm in the netherworld using the Darkfyre in order to hunt Erixitl of Palul, a chosen of Qotal, whom the Ancient Ones needed to destroy in order to accomplish their plans to achieve domination over Maztica.

During the Night of Wailing, Erixitl of Palul and her companions confronted the Ancestor along with the other Ancient Ones in the Highcave near the Darkfyre. During their confrontation, Chitikas, a couatl servant of Qotal, attacked the Ancestor and plunged both of them together into the Darkfyre. Immediately following this, the Darkfyre caused Mount Zatal to explode in a massive eruption that covered the city of Nexal with ash. Lolth, whom the Ancient Ones and their ancestors had served from before the time of the Rockfire, and who had grown jealous of their betrayal of her in favor of Zaltec since their coming to Maztica, was able to use her power to corrupt the drow magic of the Darkfyre in order to cause the fire and ashes to inflict horrific transformations on the Ancient Ones, as well as on all Nexalans who had been marked with the Viperhand that were touched by the ashes. For the latter group, Zaltec actually helped along these transformations, as he found it better for his zealots to lose their humanity entirely and become murderous monsters, in order to satiate his endless hunger for bloodshed.

## Daud

Daud was a human thief and a founder and leader of the Clenched Fist, a Rundeen-affiliated mercenary and adventuring company based in Schamedar in Calimshan in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

Personality
Daud had amnesia, having no early memories apart from his name. This made him curious and driven to uncover secrets. He was also described as a "horror", given his evil ways.

Description
A long scar ran over his forehead and scalp—a likely cause of his memory loss. It turned red when he was angered.

## Dark Moon monk

Dark Moon monks were monks who followed the ways taught by the Order of the Dark Moon.

Activities
The monks followed their purpose of executing Shar's will across Abeir-Toril with single-minded devotion. They sometimes performed missionary work, attempting to teach and indoctrinate individuals they encountered on their journeys.

Membership
Being a Dark Moon monk was both a religious and martial tradition. While becoming a monk was possible through rigorous and sometimes cruel training in Dark Moon monasteries, there were also those who learned these traditions by themselves and, while having no contact with Sharran organizations, considered themselves Dark Moon monks. It required a certain type of discipline and because of that, fully immersing oneself into the Way of Shadow tradition was possible only for lawful evil individuals that wanted to follow it as monks (in contrast to shadowdancers, who were not limited by their alignment, to practice it).

Culture
These monks were prone to use deception in contact with non-Sharrans.

Abilities
Dark Moon monks were trained in detecting illusions. They learned the 'frozen fist' technique, which allowed their punches to deal freezing injuries. With training, they could learn the following spells: blindness, blur, vampiric touch, and mirror image. Because of their training or faith, they could not lay on healing hands or make a stunning blow.

History
The traditions and practices of the Dark Moon monks were established by 1369 DR.

These traditions continued for over a century, into the era of the Second Sundering.

Notable Members
 Hemma, a monk who was encountered by Abdel Adrian when he was young and tried to indoctrinate him but he followed a different path.

## Daikon

Daikon was a wizard with the Arcane Brotherhood of Luskan in the late 14 century DR.

Description
He wore a cowled robe.

Personality
Daikon's ambition was remarkable.

Abilities
One of his spells launched a missile of colored light. Another spell created up to four balls of light, likely dancing lights.

Possessions
He had a stone through which he sent and received messages, most likely a speaking stone.

Relationships
He served Arklem Greeth. During his mission in Ieirithymbul, he had three accomplices.

History
In Uktar of the, Daikon intercepted a caravan of gnomes in Leilon that was on its way back to Ieirithymbul and killed them, interrogating the last before killing him, and taking on the likeness of the four dead gnomes for him and his accomplices. He did this under the orders of Arklem Greeth, the Archmage Arcane, who bade him confirm the identity of the Unseen Protector of Ieirithymbul.

Once inside Ieirithymbul, Daikon and his accomplices quickly captured Kaylindrra Gromann, wife of elder Froga Gromann, and forced him to take them to the foothills of Felrenden, to a place where the Unseen Protector, the gold dragon Palarandusk, could be found. Daikon knocked out the gnome once there, and summoned Arklem Greeth. Under the Archmage Arcane's supervision, an antimagic trap was set up to capture the gold dragon Palarandusk; Daikon himself acted as additional bait, disguised as a young gnome. Palarandusk turned up, and was soon caught.

## Dallabad Oasis

Dallabad Oasis was an oasis and nearby palatial fortress in Calimshan in the Lands of Intrigue in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

Location
It lay in the Calim Desert, a short distance outside of Calimport along the northwestern trails.

Description
The oasis itself was but a collection of small ponds surrounded by a few palm trees and large boulders. Passing caravans set up their tents and pavilions close by.

From the outside, the fortress seemed equally unremarkable, appearing to be a simple square-walled fortress built of brown stone appeared to blend in with the surrounding desert sands and dunes. It was surrounded by an open field, almost a  wide, which separated it from the oasis and made it hard for infiltrators to get close unobserved.

Structure
The outer walls stood some  high, and were constructed of brown sandstone and gray-hued granite with polished white marble joints. They were quite sheer to all but the most expert climbers. The space between the walls and inner keep formed a courtyard.

The square outer walls concealed a roughly circular keep within. Its corridors wound inward in ever tighter circles, leading ultimately to its master's treasury rooms and private chambers. These halls were secured with heavy, metal-banded doors comprising layers of wood and stone that would withstand physical and even magical attack. Sturdy locks, alarms, and traps further enhanced security.

Deep tunnels ran beneath the fortress and were linked to the fortress by a long, spiral staircase.

Interior
Within, the keep was decorated with floor-to-ceiling tapestries and doors adorned with gold leaf.

Defenses
At first glance, the fortress did not appear to be very strong, nor well-defended. The robed guards patrolling the walls seemed bored by their quiet duty. In fact, the fortress's defenses were designed more to thwart thieves and protect its master's treasures. The guards were actually courageous, highly trained, and well-equipped with chainmail, bucklers, and enchanted swords. Kohrin relied on the power of Charon's Claw and of Yharaskrik to counter any magical attack.

Government
In the mid-1300s DR, Dallabad Oasis was ruled with an iron fist by Kohrin Soulez, who exploited his power over the enclosed oasis and the caravans that stopped by and slew many who displeased him. Jealously guarding his treasures and especially the evil sentient sword Charon's Claw, he remained isolated, keeping himself locked up in his fortress. The fortress was independent of Calimport's guilds as none of them had the power to take the fortress, even if two or three came together in alliance.

In order for Kohrin Soulez to run Dallabad Oasis, he had five trustworthy lieutenants with him at all times, three of which were his own children, including his daughter Ahdahnia Soulez, a fourth was a talented military commander from Memnon, and the other was a thief from Calimport named Preelio. A sixth lieutenant that only Soulez's closest commanders knew about was a mind flayer by the name of Yharaskrik, who aided in interrogation and torture but otherwise stayed apart.

After Kohrin's death in 1366 DR, it was commanded by Ahdahnia Soulez, on behalf of House Basadoni.

Activities
The Soulez clan collected tolls from caravans passing through the area. Caravans also paid for the use of water and shelter at the oasis. Caravan masters or their servants could simply pay the fortress guards. However, they tended to extort and rob those they could. The commander of the fortress also learned information from caravan masters.

Dallabad Oasis also served as a relay point for communication between Pasha Da'Daclan of Calimport and his more powerful allies far away, and Da'Daclan paid Soulez for this, whilst remaining independent.

History

At some point, the illithid known as Yharaskrik had come to Dallabad Oasis seeking to study Charon's Claw. It fought with Kohrin and pretended to be defeated by him and Charon's Claw's power, before Kohrin offered it a deal. Yharaskrik studied the Charon's Claw artifact while living in the deep tunnels below Kohrin Soulez's throne room.

For decades, Dallabad Oasis had been held by the Soulez clan. It was said that nothing had changed and nothing of note had happened at Dallabad Oasis in twenty years, as of the mid-1360s DR. That was until the, when the assassin Artemis Entreri took an interest in Dallabad Oasis and especially in Charon's Claw. Entreri's friends Jarlaxle and Sharlotta Vespers in House Basadoni sought to disrupt Pasha Da'Daclan's line of communication to his allies, and so sought to take Dallabad for themselves. Thus, launching a surprise attack during the daylight hours, Jarlaxle used the power of Crenshinibon to conjure a crystalline tower within the walls of the fortress, and Jarlaxle and Rai-guy Bondalek led a force of Bregan D'aerthe drow mercenaries to overwhelm the stunned defenders. Meanwhile, Entreri used the distraction and confusion to get over the walls and get behind Kohrin as he led a hasty defense, infiltrating the keep ahead of him. The drow used sleep poison to knock out the defenders and accepted surrenders, taking the majority alive. Having already been contacted by Kimmurel Oblodra, Yharaskrik abandoned its servitude to Kohrin as it much preferred drow to humans, and departed. Then Entreri surprised Kohrin and Ahdahnia in the throne room and the two men fought. During the battle Entreri disarmed Kohrin of Charon's Claw and the protective glove he wore, and deftly changed it for a copy. When Kohrin donned the false glove and again picked up the cursed sword, he was killed. Artemis Entreri took Charon's Claw from Kohrin Soulez's lifeless hand.

In the aftermath, Jarlaxle and Bregan D'aerthe kept Dallabad Oasis for themselves, now using it as a base and relay point for the Basadoni Guild. Ahdahnia Soulez and the many surviving guards agreed to stay on and actually run the place—the psychic power of Crenshinibon helped sway their minds and obscure their memories. This maintained appearances of a near-seamless transition of power to the outside world. Back in the tunnels, Yharaskrik allied himself with Kimmuriel Oblodra. The creature taught Kimmuriel how to prevent Crenshinibon from controlling him, thereby making Kimmuriel an ally of necessity.

Days later, rumor in the criminal underworld of Calimport was that Ahdahnia had slain her father in a coup triggered by the cursed sword, and she had sold Charon's Claw to Entreri, as he'd earlier offered to buy it from Kohrin. Nevertheless, many of those in the know were skeptical of this story and the new crystalline tower and suspected the truth. Pasha Broucalle of Memnon sent spies Lipke, Trulbul, and Rolmanet to Dallabad to observe. Jarlaxle experimented with the power the Crystal Shard even as it gained influence over him, together mind-controlling and slaying the spies. Later, Jarlaxle even erected a second crystalline tower within the fortress.

Finally, House Basadoni's covert control of Dallabad Oasis was an open secret in Calimport and Kimmuriel and Rai-guy took control of Bregan D'aerthe, owing to the Crystal Shard's influence over Jarlaxle, forcing he and Entreri to flee Dallabad Oasis whilst the crystalline towers collapsed. Dallabad Oasis remained in the clutches of House Basadoni and Bregan D'aerthe, at least until Kimmuriel and Rai-guy took their drow mercenary force back to the Underdark and killed Sharlotta Vespers, leaving the Basadoni guild in turmoil and Dallabad in the command of Ahdahnia Soulez.The actual fate of Dallabad Oasis is unclear, as Servant of the Shard has the main characters simply depart. Dallabad Oasis and the Soulezes are not mentioned again.

Notable Inhabitants
 Kohrin Soulez, commander of Dallabad Oasis and wielder of Charon's Claw and its gauntlet.
 Ahdahnia Soulez, his daughter and successor, serving Bregan D'aerthe.
 Tonakin Ta'salz, a courageous solder amongst the guards.
 Yharaskrik, a mind flayer dwelling below ground.

## Daegon

Daegon was a human druid of the Storm Horns during the late 15 century DR.

History

Around the time of the Shadovar invasion of Wheloon, the forces of Risen Netheril took over part of the Storm Horns as Archwizard Amskar built his army. They caused a good deal of environmental damage as they went, part of which fell upon the druid Daegon, who lived near Yarrow Glade with his beloved owlbears. He fought off the invaders with mounting fury and eventually began simply attacking anyone who approached, whether they were hostile or not.
